title: Comparison of the optical quality after SMILE and FS-LASIK for high myopia by OQAS and iTrace analyzer: a one-year retrospective study

license.statement: CC BY 4.0 (article <license>: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License)

indication: high myopia (inclusion: spherical refraction -6.00 to -10.00 D, astigmatism 0 to -2.50 D, age 18 years or older); retrospective single-surgeon comparison, right eyes only

groups.description: SMILE (VisuMax 500 kHz, optical zone 6.0-6.8 mm, cap 100-120 um), manufacturer nomograms without adjustment; right eyes of 51 patients
FS-LASIK (VisuMax flap 90 um, VISX Star S4 excimer), manufacturer nomograms without adjustment; right eyes of 49 patients

exclusions.what: Fig. 1 standard graphs (SE within +/-0.50 D, SE change >0.50 D, attempted versus achieved)

notes: Refraction: manifest refraction (Methods); recorded as manifest.
Target refraction not stated (manufacturer nomograms without adjustment); recorded as unstated.
Analysis set: right eyes with regular checks at 1, 6 and 12 months (attendance-based inclusion criterion, not outcome-defined; kept).
Procedure was allocated by corneal thickness, refractive error and patient preference (non-randomized).
Astigmatism, UDVA (Table 1), OQAS strehl ratio, MTF cutoff, OSI (Table 2) and iTrace wavefront aberrations (Tables 3-4) are tabulated; not extracted.

series.notes: mean ± SD (asterisks mark within-group tests); rows Post 1mo/6mo/12mo lack the spanned label cell, so the SMILE value is C2 there; all eyes had the 1, 6 and 12 month checks (inclusion criterion)
mean ± SD; the FS-LASIK value is C3 in the rows without the spanned label cell; all eyes had the 1, 6 and 12 month checks
